h: The Menorah and Sacred Eating Confront Hidden Desire

p: This too is from his holy manuscript:
In Midrash Rabbah (on this parshah, Bamidbar Rabbah 15:4):
that Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him,
and the Holy One, blessed be He, showed him, etc.;
from the wording of the verse (Bamidbar 8:4):
"according to the vision that He showed," etc.,
Now what is the allusion in this,
in the three times that he had difficulty?
what connection does this have to here?
at the making of the Menorah.
the matter of what it said,
shall the seven lamps give light"
according to the exposition of our Sages, of blessed memory,
And one may say, by way of the plain meaning,
that the Menorah is in the south,
and "toward the face of the Menorah"
"From the north the evil will open";
and "the heart of the fool is to his left."
in the words of our Sages, of blessed memory,
is said of one who goes in an evil way,
those who go in a good way.
"the heart of the wise man is to his right
and the heart of the fool to his left" (Koheles 10:2);
they learned from this also regarding the kidneys:
that the right one counsels him for good, etc.
And north is to the left
when a person stands facing east;
for that is why east is called kedem, "front."
of the seven names of the evil inclination
because it is hidden in one's heart;
against Torah scholars more than all;
corresponding to seven levels of holiness;
exists even in one who is completely clean:
as long as there has not been rectified
the sin of Adam HaRishon completely,
there is still existence to the evil inclination.
As with King David, peace be upon him,
"And my heart is slain within me"
that he slew the evil inclination through fasting;
at the time of the trial
for "God made one opposite the other" (Koheles 7:14);
For Adam HaRishon before the sin
did not sense his own pleasure;
וְכֵן אִיתָא בְּיַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
and so it says of Yaakov Avinu, peace be upon him (Rashi Bereishis 29:21);
and so it says of the future:
And therefore it says in the Sifrei:
only out of eating and drinking,"
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּפָרָשַׁת וָאֶתְחַנַּן (דְּבָרִים ו, יא-יב)
"And you will eat and be sated;
"Lest you eat and be sated," etc.,
and there at the end of the parshah (Devarim 11:15–16):
"And you will eat and be sated;
"And it will eat and be sated and grow fat,
in the name of a midrash:
that words of Torah enter your innards,
And this refers to permitted eating:
whatever is to fill his belly
and not with intention for the sake of Heaven.
And words of Torah break the inclination,
that one must ask for this more,
for the beginning of Adam HaRishon's sin
and the entry of the inclination
was through the desire for eating,
and it brought into his heart the sensation of desire,
its first entry into the heart.
the Table is in the north:
And to this they alluded in the Zohar,
"'May He send your help from the Sanctuary' (Tehillim 20:3)
this is the washing of hands;
'May He grant you according to your heart.'
for in Shocher Tov on Psalm 20,
"May He grant according to your heart,"
that this may not be said
except to one whose heart is whole with Hashem;
And for this it said beforehand
for "your meal offerings and your burnt offering" (Tehillim 20:4)
that his eating should be like offerings;
was like offering the daily offerings;
like pouring a libation of wine;
'she shall eat of her father's bread'" (Vayikra 22:13);
"Do not desire the table of kings,
for your table is greater than their table,
and your crown greater than their crown."
And his words are not to be taken literally:
that one should desire a royal table
and also, what is it that he said,
And if he alluded to the World to Come,
there is no comparison at all
to say that this is greater than that;
and also, what does "your crown," etc.,
that the crown of the Table
and we did not find more.
